Thanks for the clarification on the useMemo behavior.

Regarding the second part of the issue, do you have any insights on why the
compiler fails to memoize anything at all when all variables are inlined,
as shown in this example?

function useTranslate(getNamespace) {
  return createTranslateFunction(getNamespace(useMessages()),
useIcuFormatter());
}

In this case, the output doesn't seem to apply any memoization.


On Mon, Jun 22, 2026, 10:41 PM MaxwellCohen ***@***.***>
wrote:

> *MaxwellCohen* left a comment (react/react#36847)
> <https://github.com/react/react/issues/36847#issuecomment-4775373935>
>
> If you were to use useMemo on createTranslateFunction in the example hook,
> it would look like this:
>
> function useTranslate(getNamespace) {
>   const messages = useMessages();
>   const formatIcu = useIcuFormatter();
>
>   return useMemo(
>   () => createTranslateFunction(getNamespace(messages), formatIcu),
>    [getNamespace, messages, formatIcu]
>  );}
>
> Memoizing the result ofgetNamespace(messages) is redundant because we are
> just passing the result to createTranslateFunction, and we do not need to
> save the incremental values.
>
